extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML/PDF figures and result/discussion text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Phibilin damages C. albicans plasma membrane integrity as supported by PI uptake microscopy and quantified fluorescence-positive-cell results.

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Figure 3/result text reports increased PI-positive cells after Phibilin treatment.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Directly supports membrane permeabilization/integrity damage; it does not by itself prove a single exclusive killing pathway.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Phibilin interacts with DNA in a gel-retardation assay using plasmid and salmon sperm DNA substrates.

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Figure 5/result text supports DNA interaction without sequence-specific binding claims.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports direct DNA interaction in vitro; downstream cellular target specificity remains contextual.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Phibilin increases ROS, disrupts mitochondrial membrane potential, and shifts C. albicans cells toward necrosis in flow-cytometry assays.

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Figure 6/result and discussion text support ROS-related necrosis and mitochondrial membrane potential disruption.

mechanism_claims.limitations: The source supports a ROS-related necrosis pathway, not a complete molecular target map.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Phibilin inhibits C. albicans biofilm formation and reduces mature biofilm biomass in dose-responsive XTT/microscopy assays.

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Figure 7/result text reports biofilm inhibition and mature-biofilm reduction.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm effects are curated as phenotypic activity rather than a standalone molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Phibilin inhibits C. albicans yeast-to-hyphal transformation and damages budding-site morphology.

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Figures 4 and 8/result text support budding-site disruption and hyphal-growth inhibition.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Curated as morphology/virulence context; not over-promoted to an exclusive primary killing mechanism.
